_comment: The tool versions conformance has actually PROVEN, and the state the daily
version watch compares npm against. `version-watch.sh` reads it; the
workflow's `record` job writes it back after a passing run, so a commit here
means a chain went green at that version on that date — never that someone
harness: 'supported' = the tool is in scripts/conformance/lib/tools.sh and
the canary may dispatch a run for it. 'pending' = listed so the watch can
still report a release, but never dispatched, because run-chain.sh would
version: null = never proven. First sight RECORDS and does not dispatch —
a version nobody has tested is not a change, and the same forward-only rule

claude_code.proven_by: local host run on darwin/arm64: make conformance TOOL=claude_code, five checkpoints
